candidates: When a refactor renames parameters (e.g. to clarify their roles), check whether any logic referencing those parameters by position or index also needs updating — a parameter rename that silently changes which entity's property (such as `.branch`) is used in a comparison is a semantic change, not a cosmetic one, and must be explicitly flagged and justified in the PR.

Every new or modified conditional branch in arrow-routing and colour-selection logic in `gitGraphRenderer.js` (e.g. in `drawArrow` or helper predicate functions) must be covered by at least one e2e snapshot test; when reviewing, verify that each predicate's true-returning path is actually reachable in practice and flag any branch that has no test exercising it.

When iterating over an object's entries to access properties on each value, use `Object.values()` rather than `Object.entries()` — `Object.entries()` yields `[key, value]` array pairs, so accessing a named property directly on the iterator element (e.g. `element.branch`) returns `undefined` instead of the expected value.

Helper functions in `gitGraphRenderer.js` that already close over module-level state (such as `commitPos` and `dir`) should derive all dependent values internally rather than accepting pre-computed derivatives as explicit parameters; prefer a minimal signature of source-data arguments and perform lookups (e.g. `commitPos[commit.id]`) inside the function body, rather than mixing implicit closure access with explicit position arguments.
